newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the settlement of contentious political issues between Islamabad and New Delhi was a pre-requisite for expanding Pak-India trade and bilateral economic relations.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif leaves on a four-day official visit of Malaysia with a 75-member delegation of businessmen.

- Opposition Pakistan People's Party has filed a reference with Chief Accountability Commissioner against Senator Saifur Rehman on alleged tax evasion in the import of 25 BMW cars in 1992 through under-invoicing.
- The federal cabinet has approved a proposal for a four percent cut in the prices of drugs to bring them at par with those prevailing in India, officials said.
- Pakistan and the United Nations will resume their joint efforts on Thursday for promoting peace and paving the way for an intra-Afghan dialogue.

- The IMF has linked the disbursement of the first tranche of $200 million from the proposed $1.6 billion three-year Extended Structural Adjustment Facility loan to five major conditions including land reforms and opening of the services sector to foreign investors.

- The finance ministry has asked the government to guarantee a bank loan of $100 million in Pakistani rupees to Water and Power Development Authority to enable it to pay back a loan obtained from Societe Generale which is maturing on Thursday.
- Privatisation Commission has invited expression of interest from private investors for the sale of 51 percent shares of First Women Bank, an official announcement said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has asked the Privatisation Commission to prepare a new list of state-owned units to be privatised and present their sale schedule to the cabinet.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has made changes in the export Finance Scheme by including more commodities in the list for the export refinance facility.
